config.name: g1-short-forward-pass
config.description:
The experiment G1 has been waiting for. NIGHT-REPORT §8 is blunt about it: "The G1 mechanism was never actually stressed — no configuration tested decoded faster than 36.8 ms/token."
G1's mechanism is that CPU-side grammar mask construction cannot hide behind the GPU forward pass when the forward pass is short. Every model measured so far decodes at 36.8-65.7 ms/token, which leaves ample room to hide a mask costing tens of microseconds. XGrammar claims <40 us/token; against a 37 ms forward pass that is ~0.1%, while the best detection floor achieved so far was 0.50%. The instrument is 5-20x too coarse at these model sizes — not because the instrument is bad, but because the models are too slow for the effect.
The fix is not a better instrument, it is a shorter forward pass. This runs the smallest current models available through Ollama, where per-token decode should fall well under 20 ms and the mask can no longer hide.
Several tags are listed deliberately: the runner pulls each and records any it cannot (003 skipped gemma3:4b for a llama.cpp load failure and recorded it rather than faking it — same behaviour applies here). Even two working small models answer the question.
Reading the result: the key column is per-token decode time and the paired gbnf-minus-unconstrained difference with its CI, exactly as in NIGHT-REPORT §7. If a positive latency tax appears here and did not at 37-66 ms/token, that is direct evidence for G1's mechanism and locates the crossover. If the tax is still absent at 10-15 ms/token, that is a strong negative result for G1 on this hardware family and it is worth saying so plainly.
